leads.tagline: Where every potential customer lives — from the first contact to the closed deal

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A lead isn't a customer yet — it's a person or company who's just showing interest: they messaged you, filled out a form on your site, called, or came in through an ad. The Leads section makes sure none of them get lost, and helps you turn them into real sales.

sections.heading: Three ways to look at your leads
bullets: Table — a full list with all fields and filters, handy when you have a lot of leads
Kanban board — cards in columns "New," "In progress," "Awaiting reply," "Deal won," "Deal lost": just drag a card into another column to change its stage
Calendar — shows scheduled meetings tied to leads; book a new meeting right here and send the customer an email invite
Custom views — save any set of filters and grouping as its own view so you can jump back to it quickly

sections.heading: Search and AI tools
bullets: Regular search — by name, phone, email, or company
Smart AI search — describe who you're looking for in plain words, like "leads from Moscow with no reply in 5 days," and the system builds the filters for you
Duplicate finder — spots leads with the same phone or email so you can merge them instead of working the same customer twice

sections.heading: Loading a lot of leads at once
sections.body: If you already have a customer list in Excel or CSV, click "Import," upload the file, and tell the system which column is which (name, phone, email, and so on). It will create the lead cards for you.

sections.heading: What you can customize
bullets: Custom fields — add your own fields to the lead card (like "Budget" or "Source") via "Customize fields"
Automations — set the system to act automatically when a lead reaches a certain stage (e.g. assign a task to a manager, or send an email)
Grouping — view leads by status, company, channel, or your own custom groups

sections.heading: How to use it — step by step
steps: Click "Create lead" and fill in a name, phone number, or email
Choose which stage the customer is currently at
Open the lead's card to add a note, assign a task, or message the customer
Once they agree to buy, move the lead to the "Deal" stage or into Sales
If they say no, mark the lead as "Lost" with a reason — this keeps your stats accurate

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Don't let a lead sit in one stage for days without any action. If nothing has happened for a while, call or message them — interest cools down fast.

leadCard.title: Lead card
leadCard.tagline: Everything about one lead lives here — contact history, tasks, and AI hints

sections.heading: What's inside the card
bullets: Basic info — name, phone, email, company, and where they came from
Custom fields — whatever you've set up for your business
History — every call, email, message, and manager's note about this lead, in one timeline
Tasks — set yourself or a teammate a reminder with a date and time
Linked projects and bookings — if there's already a deal or booking open for this customer, you'll see it right in the card

sections.heading: Moving a lead through stages
sections.body: Change the lead's status right inside the card — the same way you would on the kanban board. Do it as soon as something changes, so reports and teammates see the real picture.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: On the right side of the card there's an AI panel — a lead score, a suggested next step, and help filling in missing data. Click the "?" next to that panel to learn more about it.

leadAiTools.title: AI hints for this lead
leadAiTools.tagline: Three tools that help you quickly figure out what to do with this customer

sections.heading: Lead score
sections.body: Click "Analyze" — the AI scores the lead from 0 to 100 on how likely they are to buy, and explains what the score is based on (fast replies, asked about pricing, and so on).

sections.heading: What to do next
sections.body: The AI suggests one concrete action — call, email, or schedule a meeting — and explains why it makes sense right now.

sections.heading: Email to the customer
sections.body: You can ask the AI to draft an email to this lead — it takes the conversation history into account and gives you a ready draft to review and send.

sections.heading: Fill in missing data
sections.body: If the card is missing information, click "Enrich data" — the AI suggests values, and you apply the one you want with a single click.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: None of these hints are mandatory — they just save you time. The final call is always yours.

leadsLost.title: Lost leads
leadsLost.tagline: A report on customers who didn't end up buying — so you can see where sales are slipping away

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This lists every lead that ultimately didn't buy. It helps you see how many customers you're losing, how much revenue that represents, and which managers have the most of them — so you can fix what's going wrong.

sections.heading: What you'll see
bullets: How many leads were lost in the selected period, and for how much money
A manager comparison — who has the most lost deals
A list of every lost lead with its date and amount

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Pick a period at the top (week, month, quarter, or all time) and check whether lost leads are climbing for a particular manager — that's worth digging into.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: This is a report page — there's no button here to bring a lead back. If a lead can actually still be won, find it in the main leads list and change its status from the card.

leadsArchive.title: Lead archive
leadsArchive.tagline: Leads you've tucked away from active lists, without deleting them

sections.heading: What archiving is for
sections.body: Archiving hides a lead you don't need right now, without deleting it. For example, if the deal is on indefinite hold, or the customer asked you to check back later.

sections.heading: What you can do with an archived lead
bullets: "Restore" — bring it back to the regular lists
"Move to trash" — if it's truly no longer needed
"Delete forever" — erase it with no way back (the system asks you to confirm first)

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Archiving doesn't delete any data — use it freely whenever you're unsure if you still need a lead. You can always bring it back with one click.

leadsTrash.title: Lead trash
leadsTrash.tagline: Deleted leads stay here until you delete them for good

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: When you delete a lead, it doesn't disappear right away — it goes to the trash first. From here you can bring it back if you deleted it by mistake, or erase it permanently.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: "Restore" — bring the lead back as if nothing happened
"Delete forever" — erase it with no way back (you'll need to confirm)

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body: Leads don't leave the trash on their own — they stay until you delete them by hand. If the trash piles up, feel free to clean it out from time to time.

leadsAnalytics.title: Lead analytics
leadsAnalytics.tagline: Clear charts and numbers on how your work with customers is going

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Instead of counting things by hand in a spreadsheet, everything here is already calculated and charted: how many leads came in, how many bought, how much money you made, and which managers are performing best.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: How many leads came in over a period, and how many converted
How much revenue your won deals brought in
How fast managers respond to new leads
Where leads come from — website, social media, ads, and so on
The sales funnel — where in the process you're losing the most customers
A manager leaderboard — who's closing the most deals and revenue

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Pick a ready-made view at the top — "Overview," "Sources," "Managers," or "Funnel" — or build your own set of charts by adding and removing widgets.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the "Funnel" view once a week — it's the fastest way to spot where customers most often drop off.

leadsRoi.title: Revenue by lead
leadsRoi.tagline: How much money each lead ended up bringing in

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows more than just how many leads you had — it shows how much real revenue each one brought the company, through sales or projects. It helps you see which customers and managers are the most profitable.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Total revenue for the period and the average deal size
Your top leads by revenue
A full table per lead — manager, channel, number of deals, total amount

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Switch between "By sales" and "By projects" mode depending on what you want to measure, and pick a period at the top.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body: This tracks revenue that came from a lead, not ad spend — it's not an ad-spend-payback calculator, it's a report on which customers brought in the most money.

aiAssistant.title: Lumiva AI assistant
aiAssistant.tagline: A smart assistant built into the CRM that helps you get routine work done faster

sections.heading: What it's for
sections.body: Think of it as an extra team member who never gets tired. Tell it what you need in plain words, and it can answer questions, do the math, find information, or even do part of the work for you — fill in fields, find customers, draft an email.

sections.heading: What it can do
bullets: Answer questions about your customers, deals, and sales in plain language
Find leads or contacts from a description — like "show leads from Moscow with no reply in 5 days"
Help you draft emails and messages to customers
Take an uploaded file (a spreadsheet or list) and quickly turn it into leads or deals
Remember important facts about your company in the "Memory" tab, so you don't have to repeat yourself
Take voice commands instead of typing

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Click the AI assistant icon to open the chat window
Type your question or task in plain words — like you're messaging a colleague
To attach a file, click the paperclip and pick a file from your computer
The "Memory" tab holds what the assistant has learned about your company — you can add or remove facts yourself
If you run out of the free quota, you can connect your own OpenAI key to use it without limits

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The more specific your question, the more useful the answer. Instead of "show me leads," try "show me leads that haven't replied in over a week."

projects.title: Projects
projects.tagline: Where you run the actual work with a customer — from kickoff to a closed deal

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Once a lead becomes a real customer and the work begins — a deal, an order, a service — a project is opened. Here you can see what stage each piece of work is at, who's handling it, and how much money it's worth.

sections.heading: Three ways to look at your projects
bullets: Table — a full list with all fields, filters, and grouping
Kanban board — cards in columns "New," "In progress," "Under review," "On hold," "Closed," "Won," "Lost": drag a card into another column to change its status
Calendar — shows task deadlines by date, so nothing important slips by

sections.heading: What you can customize
bullets: Custom fields — add your own fields to the project card for your business
Automations — have the system act automatically when a project's status changes
Custom views — save a set of filters and grouping so you can jump back to it quickly

sections.heading: Bulk actions
sections.body: Select several projects at once with checkboxes, then change their status, archive them, or delete them in one click.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the "On hold" column regularly — that's usually where projects quietly get forgotten.

projectCard.title: Project card
projectCard.tagline: Everything about one project — tasks, budget, files, and conversations — in one place

sections.heading: What's inside the card
bullets: Tasks — a checklist for the project: add items, assign an owner, set a deadline and priority, mark them done
Metrics — budget, task completion percentage, project priority
Notes and tags — free-form notes and labels for quick searching
Custom fields — whatever you've set up for your business
Files — links to the contract, brief, or other project documents
Comments and history — discussion with your team plus a log of every change: who changed the status, amount, or owner, and when

sections.heading: Links to other sections
sections.body: The card shows which lead the project came from and which company it belongs to. You can send an email to the customer right from here, and if Jira is connected, link a developer ticket to it.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The tasks inside the card are a checklist, not a board: to reorder them, drag the individual task, not the whole card.

projectsArchive.title: Project archive
projectsArchive.tagline: Projects you've tucked away from active lists, without deleting them

sections.heading: What archiving is for
sections.body: Archiving hides a project you don't need right now, without deleting it — for example, if the work is on indefinite hold.

sections.heading: What you can do with an archived project
bullets: "Restore" — bring it back to the regular lists
"Delete" — move it to the trash

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Archiving doesn't delete any data — use it freely whenever you're not sure if you still need a project right now.

projectsTrash.title: Project trash
projectsTrash.tagline: Deleted projects stay here until you delete them for good

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: When you delete a project, it doesn't disappear right away — it goes to the trash first. From here you can bring it back if you deleted it by mistake, or erase it permanently.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: "Restore" — bring the project back as if nothing happened
"Delete forever" — erase it with no way back

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body: Projects don't leave the trash on their own — they stay until you delete them by hand.

projectsClosed.title: Closed projects
projectsClosed.tagline: Every project that's reached an outcome — won, lost, or simply closed

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This lists projects with the status "Closed," "Won," or "Lost" — meaning the work on them is done. It's a handy place to check when reviewing results for a period.

sections.heading: What you'll see
bullets: How many projects are closed and their total value
A breakdown by category and by who ran the project
The full list of closed projects in a table

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Compare these numbers month to month — it's the easiest way to spot whether the business is growing or slowing down.

projectsInProgress.title: Projects in progress
projectsInProgress.tagline: A quick slice: only the projects that are currently active

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is the same project list, already filtered down to only those with the status "In progress." Handy when you want to focus on current work without closed or not-yet-started projects getting in the way.

sections.heading: What you'll see
bullets: How many projects are currently active, and their total value
A breakdown by category
The full list of active projects in a table

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check this page at the start of the day — it's the fastest way to see what your team is actually working on right now.

projectsTasks.title: Project tasks
projectsTasks.tagline: Every task from every project, in one shared list

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Instead of opening each project one by one, all tasks from every project are gathered here. It's a quick way to see the team's whole to-do list at a glance.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Add a new task with an owner, deadline, and priority
Mark a task done with one click
Reassign the owner
Click the task's project to open it

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Use the status filter and search by owner to quickly find just your own tasks in the shared list.

projectsOverdue.title: Overdue tasks
projectsOverdue.tagline: A report on tasks whose deadline has passed and still aren't done

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows every task that was supposed to be finished by a certain date but still isn't marked done — sorted by how overdue it is.

sections.heading: What you'll see
bullets: The task and which project it belongs to
The owner and priority
The deadline and how many days it's overdue

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Click the project name to jump straight to its card and figure out why the task stalled.

projectsAnalytics.title: Project analytics
projectsAnalytics.tagline: Clear charts and numbers on how project work is going

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Instead of counting things by hand in a spreadsheet, everything here is already calculated and charted — how many projects are running, for how much money, and in which categories.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Total project count and value, plus the average deal size
A breakdown by status, category, and project owner
A full projects table, plus pivot tables for deeper analysis

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Build your own set of charts — add, remove, and resize widgets, and pick a period at the top, including a custom date range.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Start with the built-in status and category blocks — that's usually enough to get the overall picture without building analytics from scratch.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.tagline: Every person you deal with, no matter what stage a deal is at

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A contact is a specific person — a customer, a partner, or someone at a client company. Unlike a lead, a contact stays in your database forever, even after a deal is closed, so you keep the full history of dealing with that person.

sections.heading: What you can do here
bullets: Search contacts by name, phone, email, or company
Group the list by company, status, owner, or your own custom groups
Reorder and resize the table columns to your liking
Select several contacts at once and change their owner, status, or add a tag in one action

sections.heading: Adding a contact
sections.body: Click "Create contact" and fill in the name, phone, email, company (you can create a new one on the spot), and the rest of the fields. You can assign it to one or more owners right away.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If the same person ended up in your database twice, check "Find duplicates" — the system will spot similar cards for you.

contactCard.title: Contact card
contactCard.tagline: One person's profile — their details, company, and related deals

sections.heading: What's inside the card
bullets: Basic info — phone (with a quick "send SMS" button), email, job title, city, country, LinkedIn, Telegram
Company — the linked company shows right here; click through to it in one tap
"Leads" tab — every lead tied to this person
"Projects" tab — every project that grew out of those leads

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a contact changes company or job title, update the card right away, so their whole deal history stays attached to the right person.

companies.title: Companies
companies.tagline: Every organization you work with, and the stats behind each one

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A company gathers all the contacts, leads, and projects for one client organization in one place — handy when you're dealing with several people at the same company.

sections.heading: What you can do here
bullets: Search and filter companies by status
Switch between table view and card view
Select several companies at once and change their owner, status, or add a tag in one action
Jump straight from the list to a company's own task board

sections.heading: Adding a company
sections.body: Click "Create company" and fill in the name, contact details, website, industry, and company size.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Fill in "Company size" — it's a quick way to gauge how big a client is at a glance from the list.

companyCard.title: Company card
companyCard.tagline: Everything about one client organization — contacts, deals, tasks, and analytics

sections.heading: What's inside the card
bullets: Summary — how many contacts, leads, and projects are tied to this company, and the potential revenue
"Contacts" tab — everyone at this company in your database
"Leads" and "Projects" tabs — every deal and piece of work tied to the company
"Tasks" tab — tasks across all of the company's projects, with a link to the full task board
"Analytics" tab — conversion rate and average project value for this company specifically

sections.heading: AI assistant
sections.body: The "Enrich data" button lets AI suggest and fill in missing company fields (website, industry, and more) once you've given it at least a little information to work from.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Start working with a new organization from its company card — that way all its people, deals, and tasks end up in one place from day one.

companiesAnalytics.title: Company analytics
companiesAnalytics.tagline: Which of your client companies bring in the most revenue

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows which companies are your biggest and most valuable clients, by number of deals and by money.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Total companies, leads, projects, and revenue in your database
Charts of top companies by revenue and by number of projects
A top-10 leaderboard of the most profitable companies, linking to each one's card

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the top-10 list at least once a month — these are your most valuable clients, worth treating with extra care.

companyTasks.title: Company task board
companyTasks.tagline: A kanban board with the tasks from every project at one company

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If a company has several projects running at once, this lets you see all their tasks on one board instead of jumping between each project's card.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Drag a task between "To do," "In progress," "Review," "Done," and "Cancelled" to change its status
Create a new task and assign an owner, priority, and deadline right away
Filter the board by text, priority, owner, and due date — overdue, today, this week

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Use the "Overdue" filter to instantly see what's stuck for this client.

duplicates.title: Duplicate finder
duplicates.tagline: Finds matching records that accidentally ended up in your database twice

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Over time your database can pick up duplicates — for example, the same customer submitting a form twice. This section finds those pairs and helps you merge them.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Check for duplicates across contacts, leads, companies, sales, and segments — switch between the tabs
Click "Run scan" and the system shows you similar pairs with a match percentage
Merge a pair into one record, or mark it as "not a duplicate"

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Run a scan once a month, especially after a big list lands in your database from an import or a web form.

sales.title: Sales
sales.tagline: Every order that came in through your connected sales channels

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Unlike leads and projects, a sale is already a finished order that arrived automatically from a connected source — an online store, a booking system, or another channel. This is where you see every order in one place.

sections.heading: What you can do here
bullets: Search orders and filter them by date, status, or channel
Reorder and resize the table columns to your liking
See a summary for each status — how many orders and for how much

sections.heading: Order statuses
sections.body: Every order moves through statuses: New, Pending, Confirmed, Cancelled, Refunded, Other — an easy way to track where payment and fulfillment stand.

sections.heading: What you can customize
bullets: Custom fields — add your own fields to the order card for your business
Automations — have the system act automatically when an order's status changes
Import — if you already have a list of orders in Excel or CSV, upload it as one file

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If you don't see any orders at all, check "Integrations" — chances are a sales channel hasn't been connected yet.

saleCard.title: Order card
saleCard.tagline: Everything about one order — items, payment, customer, and status

sections.heading: What's inside the card
bullets: The order's status and amount, plus the channel it came from
Order contents — what products or services the customer bought
Customer details and a "Create payment link" button if payment hasn't gone through yet
Custom fields and notes for your own notes on the order

sections.heading: Link to leads
sections.body: If the order came from a customer already in your database as a lead, the card shows that link. If there's no lead yet, you can create one right from here without switching sections.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If Jira is connected for this customer, you can link a developer ticket to the order right away, without opening another service.

salesChannels.title: Sales channels
salesChannels.tagline: The sources your orders come in through

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A sales channel is a specific source of orders — for example, direct sales, a travel agency (B2B), an online booking platform (OTA), or a distribution system (GDS). Every order is tied to its channel, so you can see where your sales are coming from.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: See, for each channel, how many orders came in, total revenue, and the last sync time
Turn a channel on or off
Delete a channel you no longer need

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Channels themselves are created on the Integrations page — this page is where you come to manage them afterward.

salesPayments.title: Payments
salesPayments.tagline: A ledger of every payment attempt on your orders through connected payment providers

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This gathers every payment attempt on your orders — successful, failed, and pending — through your connected payment providers.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: A list of every payment with the buyer, amount, status, and provider
A summary — how many payments succeeded, how many are pending, how many failed
A 30-day trend chart and a breakdown by provider
A list of recent failed payments with the failure reason

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Click a payment to jump straight to the order it belongs to.

salesIntegrations.title: Sales integrations
salesIntegrations.tagline: Connect the sources your orders will arrive from automatically

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: For orders from your online store or another system to land in the CRM automatically instead of being entered by hand, you need to connect an integration.

sections.heading: What you can connect
bullets: WooCommerce — a WordPress-based online store: you'll need the site URL and API access keys
Manual — if there's no ready-made connection, orders can be entered or uploaded yourself

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Pick an integration type, name it, optionally attach it to a sales channel, and enter the connection details. Once saved, you can test the connection and trigger a manual sync.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Keep an eye on the last-sync status in the list — if it hasn't updated in a while, orders may have stopped coming in.

salesImport.title: Order import
salesImport.tagline: Upload a ready-made list of orders as a file, instead of entering each one by hand

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If you already have a list of orders in Excel or CSV — say, an export from another system — you don't have to enter them by hand, you can upload the whole file.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Upload your orders file
Match the file's columns to the system's fields — order number, product, amount, date, customer, and so on; the system suggests a mapping automatically
Review the result and confirm the import

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If you've set up custom fields for orders, you can map those to file columns during import too.

products.title: Products
products.tagline: The catalog of everything you sell — prices, stock, and categories

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This holds every product or service you sell, with its price, photo, category, and stock level. The catalog is used inside the CRM — for example, when building an order — and can also be shown to customers on your website.

sections.heading: What you can do here
bullets: Search products and filter by category and status — active, draft, archived, out of stock
Switch between table view and card view
Select several products at once and change their status, category, or send them to print labels in one action
Export the catalog to CSV, Excel, or PDF

sections.heading: What you see for each product
sections.body: A photo, name, SKU, category, price, margin, and a stock bar — a yellow or red bar tells you right away when a product is running low.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Watch the tiles at the top of the page — "Low stock" and "Out of stock" show you what needs restocking.

productCard.title: Product card
productCard.tagline: Everything about one product — price, stock, photos, and variants

sections.heading: Basic info
bullets: Name, photo, SKU, barcode (with a live preview of how it looks), description
Price and cost price — margin is calculated automatically; you can set a sale price for a specific date range
Stock level and a "low stock" threshold, weight, and dimensions
Tags — for quick search and grouping

sections.heading: Product variants
sections.body: If a product comes in different sizes or colors, turn on variants — pick the attributes you need (like "Size" and "Color"), and the system generates every combination with its own SKU, price, and stock.

sections.heading: Showing it on your website
sections.body: In the "Public catalog" section you can send a product to your storefront — the request goes for review first, and the product goes live once approved.

sections.heading: Other tabs
bullets: Attributes — the values of your own custom fields, set up in "Field types"
Codes — the product's QR code and barcode, with a quick shortcut to print labels
History — who changed which field, and when

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: You can build a product out of other products as a "bundle" — turn on the "Bundle" toggle and list what's inside with quantities.

productCategories.title: Product categories
productCategories.tagline: The sections your catalog is grouped into

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Categories help structure your catalog — for example, "Clothing" → "Jackets." Each category can have its own color for quick recognition in lists.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Create categories and nested subcategories — one level of nesting
Set a name, a short URL slug, and a color
See how many products are in each category

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Don't build too many levels — one category plus one subcategory is usually enough to keep the catalog easy to navigate.

productAttributes.title: Attributes and field types
productAttributes.tagline: Two different tools for describing products — here's the difference

sections.heading: Attributes — for product variants
sections.body: An attribute is a list of values that variants are built from. For example, a "Color" attribute with Red/Blue/Green lets you set up one "T-shirt" product in three colors, each with its own SKU, price, and stock.

sections.heading: Field types — for describing a product
sections.body: Field types is a builder for your own custom product properties: text, number, date, dropdown, color, image, a link to another record, and more. These fields show up on the "Attributes" tab of a product's card and let you store whatever data matters for your business.

sections.heading: Which one to use
sections.body: If a value should create a separate product with its own price and stock — size, color — use "Attributes." If it's just extra information about the product — material, country of origin, warranty — use "Field types."

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Group your fields into named sections under "Field types" — that keeps the "Attributes" tab on a product card tidy instead of one long list.

productStock.title: Stock levels
productStock.tagline: How much of each product you have right now, and where

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows the exact quantity of every product (or variant) in stock, broken down by location if you have more than one.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Search for a product and turn on the "Low stock only" filter
"Adjust" — add or subtract a quantity at a chosen location, with an optional reason
"Transfer" — move a quantity from one location to another

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Always note a reason when adjusting stock down — a month later you'll be able to tell whether it was a sale, damage, or a stock count.

productLocations.title: Locations
productLocations.tagline: The places you store stock, so you can move it between them

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If you have more than one storage point — a warehouse, a shop, a showroom — set them up here, so you can see stock for each location separately.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Add a location with a name and an optional code
Turn a location on or off
Set a location as "default" — a default location can't be deactivated or deleted

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If you only have one point of sale, you don't need separate locations — stock totals still work correctly without them.

productFeeds.title: Product feeds
productFeeds.tagline: Ready-made links that hand your catalog to external services

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A feed is an automatically updated file with your whole catalog, in a format external services understand — Google Shopping, WooCommerce, or any other system via a generic JSON feed.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Copy the feed link for a given site with one click
Use it when setting up Google Shopping ads or moving your catalog into another system

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The link always reflects current data — there's no manual feed refresh, just paste it once into the destination service.

productWebhooks.title: Product webhooks
productWebhooks.tagline: A technical feature — notifications about catalog events for other systems

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A webhook is an automatic notification the CRM sends to an address you choose whenever something happens to a product: it's created, updated, deleted, its stock changes, or it's published.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Add a webhook — give it a name and a target URL to send notifications to
Turn a webhook on or off, and regenerate its signing secret
View a log of every notification sent — which succeeded and which failed

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: You only need this section if you (or your developer) are connecting the CRM to another system — like a warehouse app or your own website. It's not needed for everyday product management.

productModeration.title: Product moderation
productModeration.tagline: Reviewing products before they go live on your website

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: When you request to publish a product to your website from its card, the request lands here for review instead of going live instantly — a safety net against pricing, photo, or description mistakes.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: See every product waiting to be published
Approve — the product goes live on your site right away
Reject with a reason — the author sees what needs fixing

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If you work alone and publish your own products, just approve them right away — this step doesn't have to slow you down.

productsAnalytics.title: Product analytics
productsAnalytics.tagline: How much your stock is worth, and which products earn you the most

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows the health of your whole catalog — how much money is tied up in stock, your average markup, and which products you should sell off or restock.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Total catalog value at cost and at sale price, and average margin
Value broken down by category and by currency
Products with the lowest stock, and products that are out of stock
Your most valuable products by stock value

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Filter by date range, category, or location, or build your own set of charts in "Builder" mode.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the "Out of stock" list regularly — it's the most common reason for missed sales.

productImport.title: Product import
productImport.tagline: Upload your whole catalog as one file instead of entering it by hand

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If you already have a list of products in Excel or CSV, you don't have to enter each one by hand — upload the whole file.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Upload your products file
Match the file's columns to the system's fields — name, price, SKU, stock, and so on; unmatched columns can be turned into new custom fields
Choose whether to update existing products or only create new ones, and confirm the import

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: After uploading, check the results summary — how many products were created, how many updated, and whether there were any errors.

productLabels.title: Print labels
productLabels.tagline: Print price labels with barcodes for the products you select

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This prints a sheet of labels for the products you checked off in the main list — name, price, and a barcode on each one.

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: How many labels per row on the printed sheet
How many copies to print for each product

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a product has no barcode set on its card, the label shows "no barcode" instead — add one to the card ahead of time.

bookings.title: Bookings — overview
bookings.tagline: The module's home screen: what's happening with bookings today

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is the starting page of the Bookings module — it shows what's happening right now: how many bookings, how many are waiting for confirmation, and how busy your staff are.

sections.heading: What you see
bullets: Today's booking count, how many are pending confirmation, average staff workload, and the no-show rate for the last week
A time-ordered list of today's bookings — click to open one
Each staff member's workload for today
A getting-started checklist — create a service, add staff, make your first booking

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The "New booking" button takes you to the Reservations page, where bookings are actually created — it's not a separate form on this page.

reservations.title: Reservations
reservations.tagline: Every customer booking for a service, in one list

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This gathers every booking: who's booked, for which service, with which staff member, and at what time.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Jump between ready-made tabs — All, Today, Tomorrow, This week, Awaiting confirmation, Cancelled, My bookings
Filter by location, service, staff, status, and source — website, phone, walk-in, and more
Search by customer name or phone
Select several bookings and confirm or cancel them at once
Export the list to CSV, or upload bookings as a file

sections.heading: Customer card
sections.body: Clicking a customer's name opens a side panel with their visit count, total spend, tags, and last visit — no need to switch sections.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The "New booking" button opens a quick form right here — you don't have to leave the page to book a customer.

reservationCard.title: Booking card
reservationCard.tagline: Everything about one booking — service, customer, status, and history

sections.heading: What's inside the card
bullets: Overview — service, duration, location, staff, participant count, price, payment status, and source
Client — how many times they've visited, cancelled, no-showed, and their lifetime spend
Booking form data — if the customer booked through your website and filled in extra fields
History — when the booking was created, its status changes, reschedules, and notifications sent
Notes — free-form notes for your team

sections.heading: Managing status
sections.body: The buttons on the card change with the booking's status: confirm, check in, complete, mark no-show, cancel, or reject. Use the edit button to change the time, staff, resource, or payment.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Mark no-shows honestly — that data drives the no-show rate in analytics, which in turn tells you whether it's worth requiring a deposit.

reservationsImport.title: Booking import
reservationsImport.tagline: Upload a ready-made list of bookings as a file

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If you already have a list of bookings in another program or spreadsheet, bring them in here as a file instead of entering each one by hand.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Drag a CSV or Excel file into the upload area
Match the file's columns to the system's fields — the system suggests a mapping automatically
If some rows don't have a location, pick a default location to use for them
Confirm the import and check the report — how many bookings were created, and any errors

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the error report after uploading — errors are usually caused by a bad date format or a service that doesn't exist.

bookingLocations.title: Locations
bookingLocations.tagline: The branches, studios, or venues where bookings take place

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A location is a specific branch, studio, or service point. If you have more than one address, set them up here so you can run a schedule for each one separately.

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: Name, address, phone, email, and time zone
Each location has its own stats — staff, resources, today's bookings, occupancy, and revenue

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If you only have one location, set it up anyway — it doesn't add complexity, and reports work correctly with it in place.

bookingServices.title: Services
bookingServices.tagline: What customers can book — with its own price and duration

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A service is what the customer books: a haircut, a consultation, a training session, and so on. This is where you describe everything you offer.

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: Name, category, and a calendar color
Duration and price
Maximum participants per slot, and a minimum notice period
Which staff members can perform it
Whether bookings confirm automatically or need manual approval

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Give service categories different colors — it makes the schedule far easier to read at a glance.

bookingResources.title: Resources
bookingResources.tagline: Rooms, equipment, and other things that can be booked too

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A resource isn't a staff member or a service — it's a specific thing or place: a room, table, office, piece of equipment, or parking spot, tied to a location.

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: Name, type, and location of the resource
Quantity — if you have several identical resources, like five tables
Capacity and active/disabled status

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The table shows today's utilization and the next upcoming booking for each resource — a quick way to see whether a room is free right now.

bookingAvailability.title: Availability
bookingAvailability.tagline: Staff schedules, days off, and managing open slots

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is where you set exactly when customers can book: working hours, days off, and each staff member's personal schedule.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: See each staff member's hour-by-hour availability for a chosen day, and book a slot right from an open one
Set working hours per location, for each day of the week
Mark days off or closed dates for a location
Add time off or vacation for a specific staff member
Pause new bookings entirely for a while
Move all of one staff member's future bookings to another — for example, if they're out sick

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a staff member is going on vacation, add it to their schedule here right away instead of cancelling their bookings one by one.

bookingSettings.title: Booking settings
bookingSettings.tagline: General rules for the module — from confirming bookings to connecting your website

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: General — name, time zone, currency
Business type — salon, restaurant, fitness, consultations, or resource rental; this only changes the terminology, not the underlying logic
Confirmation rules — confirm bookings automatically, manually, or conditionally, for example automatically for repeat customers
Notifications — which events send an alert
Connector — an API token so a website or widget can send bookings in directly
Roles & access — which staff can do what in the module

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Start with manual confirmation until you understand your customer flow, then switch to automatic — it speeds things up once you're comfortable.

bookingWaitlist.title: Waitlist
bookingWaitlist.tagline: Customers who want to book, but there's no slot for them yet

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If a customer can't find a time that works, add them to the waitlist — as soon as a slot opens up, you offer it to them first.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Add a customer with their preferred location, service, staff member, time window, and priority
Offer a specific slot once one opens up
Turn an offer into an actual booking
Remove an entry once it's no longer relevant

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Mark VIP priority for regular customers — that way you won't forget to offer them a slot first.

bookingAnalytics.title: Booking analytics
bookingAnalytics.tagline: How busy your staff are, and how much revenue bookings bring in

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows how well your schedule is running — how many bookings, how full it is, and how many customers don't show up.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Total bookings, occupancy rate, average ticket size, and no-show rate for the chosen period
A daily booking trend and a heatmap of which days and hours get the most bookings
Customers who haven't visited in a while, with their spend and visit count
Top services by count and by revenue
Workload and revenue for each staff member
Where bookings come from — website, phone, manual, and so on

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the workload heatmap — it tells you which hours could use more staff, and which ones you could trim from the schedule.

bookingLogs.title: Event log
bookingLogs.tagline: A history of every action taken on bookings — who changed what

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This records every action taken on bookings: created, status changed, rescheduled, staff or resource changed, notification sent, note added.

sections.heading: What you'll see
bullets: The event's time, type, and a short description
A link to the booking itself — open its card directly
Who performed the action — a staff member or the system

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check here if a customer claims their time was changed without warning — the log shows exactly what happened and when.

hotels.title: Hotels — overview
hotels.tagline: The big picture across all your properties: occupancy, rates, and revenue

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: The starting page of the Hotels module — a summary of all your properties at once: how many rooms are occupied today, the average nightly rate, and last month's revenue.

sections.heading: What you see
bullets: Today's occupancy, average nightly rate, booking count, and revenue for the last 30 days
A card for each hotel — city, country, room count, current occupancy, and rate
Quick links to a hotel's pricing and markets, or to create a new one

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If you run several properties, compare their cards side by side to quickly spot which hotel is running below the others.

hotelsList.title: Hotel list
hotelsList.tagline: All your properties in one place

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is where you manage all your hotels or guest properties — whether you run just one or ten.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Search for a hotel by name or city
Create a new hotel — name, city, country, star rating, currency, address, and description
See each card's room count, room types, and current occupancy

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Click a hotel's card to open its full profile — rooms, pricing, photos, and settings.

hotelCard.title: Hotel profile
hotelCard.tagline: Everything about one property — rooms, pricing, photos, and settings

sections.heading: What's inside the profile
bullets: Rooms — room types with photos and a housekeeping status for each unit: clean, dirty, inspected, out of order
Price calendar — rates and stop-sales by date
Markets & pricing — base rates by sales channel
Hotel info — address and description
Gallery — photos organized by category
Hotel settings — including seasonal occupancy targets

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Keep an eye on housekeeping status under "Rooms" — it tells you at a glance which rooms aren't ready for a new guest.

hotelReservations.title: Hotel reservations
hotelReservations.tagline: Every room booking, across all your properties

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This gathers room bookings across all your hotels, with full financial details and a guest list for each booking.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Filter by status — confirmed, pending, checked in, checked out, cancelled
Filter by agency or sales channel
Search by guest name

sections.heading: Guest list
sections.body: Every booking has a guest manifest — one row per traveler, with name, age, citizenship, and passport number. This is specific to the hotel module.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the guest manifest ahead of time — many destinations require guest details for check-in registration.

hotelFrontDesk.title: Front desk
hotelFrontDesk.tagline: The working screen for checking guests in and out on a given day

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is the operational screen for reception staff — it shows arrivals and departures for a chosen date and hotel, and lets you check guests in or out quickly.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Pick a specific room for an arriving guest from a dropdown — occupied rooms show red, free ones green
Click "Check in" once a room is selected
Click "Check out" for today's departures in one click

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The number of guests currently in-house shows at the top of the page — a handy number to double-check at the end of a shift.

hotelPricing.title: Rates & pricing
hotelPricing.tagline: Managing room prices by market, date, and occupancy type

sections.heading: Markets & pricing
sections.body: On the "Markets & pricing" page you set the base per-person, per-night rate for each sales channel and date range — edit rates in a day-by-day grid, turn on stop-sale for specific dates, or upload rates from a file.

sections.heading: Price by room type
sections.body: On a specific room type's page, the base rate is multiplied by an occupancy coefficient — for example, single or double occupancy — to get the final room price. This page also manages that room type's photo gallery.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Start with base rates on "Markets & pricing," then fine-tune the coefficients for each room type — not the other way around.

hotelCalendar.title: Hotel calendar
hotelCalendar.tagline: Prices by date and a visual map of room occupancy

sections.heading: What's inside
bullets: "Prices & availability" tab — a calendar for setting a rate, discount, or stop-sale for each date and room type
"Room occupancy" tab — a grid where rows are physical rooms and columns are days of the month; color shows whether a room is occupied or free

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Hover over a cell in "Room occupancy" to see booking details — a quick way to gauge a whole month's occupancy at a glance.

hotelAnalytics.title: Hotel analytics
hotelAnalytics.tagline: Occupancy, average rate, and revenue — and how much more you need to sell

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows how well your hotel is filling up, whether it's hitting its revenue target, and how many rooms you need to sell today to stay on pace.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Current occupancy, rooms available, and revenue booked so far
A booking-pace chart — plan vs. actual, how much is sold by days before arrival
A revenue funnel — planned, actual, pending, and remaining
Occupancy, average rate, and revenue for each room type
Revenue broken down by market

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If the pace chart is falling behind plan, that's the moment to adjust prices or run a promotion — before arrival dates get too close.

emailAccounts.title: Mailboxes
emailAccounts.tagline: Connect your email so you can send and receive right inside the CRM

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is where you connect your work email to the CRM, so you can handle customer conversations without switching apps.

sections.heading: How to connect a mailbox
bullets: Gmail — connects in one click through your Google account
Outlook — connects in one click through your Microsoft account
Any other email — connect it manually via SMTP and IMAP settings

sections.heading: What you can configure on a connected mailbox
bullets: Sync emails manually with the "Sync now" button
Test the connection to the mail server
Set up a signature for your emails
For Gmail and Outlook — turn on auto-creating a lead from an email by an unknown sender, and a list of domains to skip

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a mailbox shows an error status, it's usually an expired password or revoked access — just reconnect it.

emailAccountForm.title: Connecting email manually
emailAccountForm.tagline: For any mailbox other than Gmail and Outlook — via SMTP and IMAP

sections.heading: Why manual setup
sections.body: If your email isn't Gmail or Outlook, connect it manually — you'll need your mail server's technical settings, usually found in your provider's help documentation.

sections.heading: What you need to enter
bullets: SMTP — server, port, username, and password for sending emails
IMAP — server, port, username, and password for receiving emails; optional, but without it emails won't load into the CRM

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: The password isn't shown when editing — leave it blank to keep the existing one, or type a new value to replace it.

emailInbox.title: Email
emailInbox.tagline: A full mailbox right inside the CRM

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Work with folders — Inbox, Sent, Trash, plus your own custom folders and subfolders
Write new emails and reply to incoming ones with attachments
Search by text, unread, starred, has a calendar invite, or has no linked lead
Send a bulk mailing from a template through the separate "Campaign" button

sections.heading: Link to leads
sections.body: If an email is from a sender the system has already matched to a lead, you'll see a link to that lead's card next to the email — the link happens automatically based on the mailbox's settings.

sections.heading: AI reply suggestion
sections.body: Next to an incoming email there's a "Suggest a reply" button — the AI reads the conversation and drafts a reply you can insert and adjust.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If an email contains a meeting invite, the CRM detects it and offers to add the meeting to your calendar in one click.

onlineChat.title: Live chat
onlineChat.tagline: Live chat from your website — talk to visitors right inside the CRM

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If a chat widget is installed on your website, every message from a visitor lands here — you can reply to customers in real time without opening a separate app.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: See a list of open conversations on the left, with the visitor's name, email, and the site they're writing from
Search conversations by keyword
Reply with text — messages refresh automatically, no page reload needed
Delete a conversation you no longer need

sections.heading: Link to leads
sections.body: If a visitor shares their contact details in the chat, the system creates a lead automatically — an "Open lead" button appears on the conversation. If there's no info yet, you'll see a "no lead yet" note.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Reply quickly — chat is usually used by customers who want an answer right now, not tomorrow.

helpdesk.title: Helpdesk
helpdesk.tagline: Every customer request, from every channel, in one list

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Helpdesk gathers customer requests into one ticket list, no matter where they came from — your website, email, a messaging app, or SMS.

sections.heading: Where tickets come from
bullets: The customer portal chat, email, Telegram, WhatsApp, SMS
A reply goes out automatically through the same channel the request came in on — the reply box shows you which one

sections.heading: What you can do with a ticket
bullets: Assign it to a staff member
Change its priority — low, medium, high, urgent
Change its status — open, pending, resolved, closed
Set a category, like "Billing" or "Account access"
Link the ticket to a lead, company, or project in the CRM

sections.heading: Tracking deadlines
sections.body: Every ticket has a target response time — if it's missed, the ticket is flagged as overdue and you'll see it right away in the list.

sections.heading: Internal staff requests
sections.body: Helpdesk can also handle internal requests — any staff member can file their own request, like a technical issue, through the notifications bell. These land in the same list, but the reply goes to the staff member as a notification instead of out to a customer by email or messaging app.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Keep an eye on the "Overdue" counter at the top of the page — the fastest way to see what needs attention right now.

esign.title: E-signatures
esign.tagline: Send documents to customers for electronic signature

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is where you write a document — a contract, an act, a power of attorney, and so on — right inside the CRM and send it to a customer for signature. There's no file to upload: the system turns your text into a PDF automatically.

sections.heading: How it works
bullets: Pick the contact who will sign the document
Optionally link the document to a lead, company, or project, so it shows up right on that record's card
Write the document text — you can use placeholders like the contact's name, email, company, and date, which fill in automatically
Click "Send" — the customer gets a link to sign

sections.heading: Document statuses
sections.body: A document moves through: draft → sent → viewed → signed. The moment the customer opens the document is tracked separately — you'll see it even before they sign. If they decline or the deadline passes, the status changes to "Declined" or "Expired."

sections.heading: Templates
sections.body: To avoid writing the same contract from scratch, save it as a template — with a name, a type (Contract, Invoice, NDA, Act, Power of attorney, Other), and body text. Pick a template when creating a new document and the text fills in automatically, ready for you to adjust for the specific customer.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a customer is taking a while to sign, send them a reminder right from the document's card, without leaving the CRM.

telephony.title: Telephony
telephony.tagline: Call customers right from the CRM — with recording and call analysis

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is where you call customers without leaving the CRM, and see the full call history — who called whom, how long, and about what.

sections.heading: How to make a call
sections.body: Type a number into the "Call" field — Twilio calls your own phone first, and once you pick up, it connects you to the customer. There's no on-screen dial pad — the call goes through your own phone.

sections.heading: What you see for each call
bullets: Direction — inbound, outbound, or missed
Duration and time of the call
A link to a lead, if the call could be matched to someone in your database

sections.heading: Call analysis
sections.body: Open a call to listen to the recording, read a text transcript, and see what the AI thinks about the conversation — sentiment (positive, neutral, negative) and topic. You can add your own tags.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a customer sounded unhappy, check the sentiment analysis in Analytics so you don't miss similar cases with other staff members.

telephonySms.title: SMS
telephonySms.tagline: SMS conversations with customers — like a messaging app

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Every SMS conversation with a customer looks like a regular chat here — a list of conversations by phone number on the left, the actual thread on the right.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Open a conversation with a given number and see its full message history
Type and send a new message right in the thread

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a message is flagged as "not delivered," check the customer's phone number — that's usually the cause.

telephonyAnalytics.title: Telephony analytics
telephonyAnalytics.tagline: How many calls and texts, which staff are busiest, and how customers feel

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Total calls and SMS, pickup rate, SMS delivery rate, and average call duration
Daily call and SMS volume over time
Workload per staff member — how many calls and messages they handled
A sentiment breakdown of calls — how many positive, neutral, and negative, and which topics cause the most frustration
Which hours of the day customers call most

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check the hourly chart to see when it's worth putting more staff on the phones.

telephonySettings.title: Telephony settings
telephonySettings.tagline: Twilio connection, staff phone numbers, and your SMS provider

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: Your Twilio connection — the credentials used for calls
The company's main number, and the list of staff numbers that receive inbound calls
Your SMS provider — Twilio, SMSC.ru, or SMS.ru — with its credentials and a sender name
Turning telephony and SMS on or off entirely

sections.heading: Recording and transcription
sections.body: Call recording and AI transcription are turned on automatically for every call and kept for 3 years — there's no separate toggle to turn them off.

sections.heading: For your developer
sections.body: This page shows the webhook URLs for inbound calls and SMS — paste them into your Twilio console once, and everything starts working.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Put whoever should receive outbound-call bridges first on the staff numbers list — that's the number Twilio dials first.

marketingTraffic.title: Traffic & channels
marketingTraffic.tagline: Where your visitors come from, and how much revenue they bring

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This gathers data from your connected ad accounts and analytics tools — Google Ads, Meta Ads, Yandex Direct, VK Ads, Google Analytics, Yandex Metrica — and shows where visitors come from and how much revenue they bring.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Impressions, sessions, clicks, leads, ad spend, and revenue for the selected period
A breakdown by data source — which tool contributed the most traffic
Top sources, mediums, and campaigns by revenue

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If this section is empty, check whether your ad accounts and analytics tools are connected in Integrations.

marketingCampaigns.title: Ad campaigns
marketingCampaigns.tagline: How each ad campaign is performing — spend, clicks, and return

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows how each individual ad campaign is performing — from Google Ads, Meta Ads, or Yandex Direct.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Impressions, clicks, sessions, and spend for each campaign
ROAS — how much revenue a campaign brought back for every dollar spent
Cost per lead (CPL), click-through rate (CTR), and cost per click (CPC)
A top-campaigns chart — compare by impressions, clicks, spend, or revenue

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If a campaign has low ROAS, compare it against your best performers on the same chart to see what's worth adjusting.

marketingBroadcasts.title: Broadcasts
marketingBroadcasts.tagline: Send a mass email or SMS to your customers

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This is where you send one message to many customers at once, by email or SMS.

sections.heading: Who to send to
sections.body: Choose "All contacts" or a specific segment — a saved group of customers from the Segments section.

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: Send right away or schedule it for a specific date and time
Build a sequence of several messages with a delay of a number of days between them
For emails — choose which mailbox to send from, and turn on open tracking

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Once a broadcast is running, watch its stats — how many were sent, how many are still queued, and how many failed.

marketingSmm.title: Social media
marketingSmm.tagline: Stats for your Instagram, Facebook, VK, Telegram, and TikTok pages

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows your social media stats in one place, instead of checking each platform separately.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Connect your Instagram, Facebook, VK, Telegram, and TikTok pages
See followers, reach, impressions, likes, comments, video views, and engagement rate
Compare stats across different periods

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body: This section only shows statistics — you can't publish or schedule posts from here, that still happens on the social platform itself.

marketingUtms.title: UTM links
marketingUtms.tagline: Build tracking links so you know exactly where a customer came from

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A UTM tag is added to a link to tell your analytics tools where the visitor came from — which ad, which email, or which post.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Pick a channel preset — Google Search, Meta Ads, Yandex Direct, Email, or Other
Fill in the campaign name, content, and keyword — the source and medium fill in automatically
Copy the finished link and use it in your ad or email
Save the link as a template so you don't have to build it again next time

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body: This page only creates links. To see how many leads and how much revenue a specific link generated, check Traffic or Campaigns instead.

marketingSegments.title: Segments
marketingSegments.tagline: Saved customer groups for broadcasts and targeting

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: A segment is a group of leads matched by conditions — for example, "new leads from Moscow in the last month." Build it once and reuse it as many times as you need.

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: Lead status, source, country, and owner
A date-created range
Specific ad campaigns from your connected Google or Meta accounts

sections.heading: How to use it
sections.body: Click "Calculate" to see how many leads match the conditions. A saved segment can then be picked as the audience when creating a broadcast.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Build segments ahead of time, before you actually need a broadcast — then sending one is just a matter of picking it from the list.

marketingSeo.title: SEO
marketingSeo.tagline: Your site's Google search rankings and load speed

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This connects to Google Search Console and Google PageSpeed Insights to show how your site is showing up in search, and how fast it loads.

sections.heading: What you can see
bullets: Clicks, impressions, CTR, and average position in Google search, with period comparison
A site speed score — performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO
Core Web Vitals — how fast and stable the page loads for real visitors

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body: This section doesn't track rankings for specific keywords or run a full site audit — it only shows data from Google Search Console and PageSpeed.

marketingEmailTemplates.title: Email templates
marketingEmailTemplates.tagline: Ready-made emails you can reuse in broadcasts and automations

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: To avoid writing the same email over and over, save it as a template — with a subject, text, and an HTML version.

sections.heading: What you can configure
bullets: Start from a ready-made preset — new lead notification, status change, new project, new sale, customer broadcast, meeting reminder, and more
Use placeholders like the lead's name, email, deal amount, or company name — they fill in automatically
Preview the email with sample data

sections.heading: Where templates are used
sections.body: Templates are used in bulk email sending and in Automations — not in Broadcasts, which has its own free-text body for each broadcast.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Set up a template with placeholders once, and it will automatically fill in the right data for every recipient.

aiEmployees.title: AI employees
aiEmployees.tagline: Virtual AI-powered team members who handle part of the work for you

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: An AI employee is a configured AI persona with a specific role, like a sales manager, that can carry out tasks in the CRM on its own — analyzing leads, drafting reports, writing emails — depending on what you allow it to do.

sections.heading: What you see
bullets: Cards for your hired AI employees — role, department, autonomy mode, and today's stats: actions taken, pending approvals, reports generated
Overall stats at the top — how many employees are active, tasks completed today, leads analyzed, issues found
A preview of pending approvals and recent activity, with links to the full pages

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Start with one AI employee in "Suggest" or "Assisted" mode — that way you see what it proposes before trusting it to act fully on its own.

aiEmployeesChoose.title: Choose a role
aiEmployeesChoose.tagline: Ready-made AI employee roles to pick from

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Before hiring a new AI employee, pick a ready-made role — for example, a sales manager. Each role already comes with a set of typical functions.

sections.heading: What you see
sections.body: A role card shows an avatar, name, a short description, and examples of what this employee can do. Some roles are limited to certain plans and show a lock icon.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Read the example functions on the card — they're the clearest sign of what this employee will actually do.

aiEmployeesCreate.title: Setting up an AI employee
aiEmployeesCreate.tagline: Step-by-step setup for a new AI employee — from role to schedule

sections.heading: Setup steps
bullets: Role — pick a ready-made template
Identity — name, avatar, language, tone of voice, department, and job title
Access — which CRM data the employee can read (leads, contacts, deals) and which actions it can take (create tasks and notes, send email and WhatsApp, change lead status)
Actions — the autonomy level: read-only, suggest, assisted, or fully autonomous, plus which actions always require your approval
Schedule — always on, business hours only, a custom schedule, or manual, plus a time for the daily report
Review — a final summary before activating

sections.heading: Changing an employee later
sections.body: The edit page only lets you change identity — name, avatar, language, tone, department, and job title. Permissions, autonomy level, and schedule are changed on the employee's own profile page, under the "Assignments" tab.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Don't grant full access right away — start with a small set of permissions and expand it once you've seen the employee handle things well.

aiEmployeesApprovals.title: Approvals
aiEmployeesApprovals.tagline: AI employee actions waiting for your decision

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: If an AI employee is only allowed to take an action with approval, it lands here and waits for a staff member to approve or reject it.

sections.heading: What you see
bullets: What action is being proposed — like sending an email, changing a lead's status, or deleting data
Which AI employee proposed it, and when
The reason the AI decided to do it

sections.heading: What you can do
sections.body: Click "Approve" to let the action run, or "Reject" if it's not needed.

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Check this list daily — while actions wait for approval, they don't run, and that can stall an employee's work.

aiEmployeesLogs.title: AI employee log
aiEmployeesLogs.tagline: Exactly what your AI employees have done, in order

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: This shows every action taken by every AI employee: what happened, who did it, and when.

sections.heading: What you'll see
bullets: The event's time and status — success, warning, or error
A short description of the action and which employee performed it
For AI-driven actions — which model was used and how many tokens it cost

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If an employee has a run of errors, check the log to see what's tripping it up before you expand its permissions.

aiEmployeesReports.title: AI employee reports
aiEmployeesReports.tagline: Reports your AI employees generate automatically

sections.heading: What this section is for
sections.body: Some AI employees generate reports on a schedule — this is where they're all collected.

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Open a report and read it in full
Check its status — sent or still pending
Mark a report as sent

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: Set the daily report time in the employee's schedule so it's ready right when your workday starts.

aiEmployeeProfile.title: AI employee profile
aiEmployeeProfile.tagline: The full profile of one AI employee — settings, stats, and history

sections.heading: What you can do
bullets: Pause or resume the employee
Run it right now, or ask it to generate a report
Edit its identity or remove it

sections.heading: Profile tabs
bullets: Overview — the role description, its functions, and today's stats
Assignments — autonomy level, permissions, approval rules, and schedule; editable right here
Approvals — this employee's own pending actions
Journal — its action history
Reports — reports generated by this employee

sections.heading: Tip
sections.body: If an employee isn't behaving as expected, pause it from the Overview tab first, then check the Journal to see what went wrong.

metaAdsAction.noConnections: No Meta Ads connection under Automations → Integrations. Needed only if you do not use the marketing integration above.
metaAdsAction.paramsJsonHint: For POST/PATCH/PUT — JSON body. Not used for GET. Placeholders {{lead.name}}, etc.
